title: An early first-passage fit gives higher density to six later large Vela glitch waits than an exponential fit
abstract: We fit two waiting-time densities to 12 early intervals between Vela glitches with fractional frequency steps of at least 1e-6. An inverse-Gaussian first-passage fit gives a mean log density gain of 0.773 nats over an exponential fit on six later intervals. Separate early and later resampling gives a central 95 percent range of 0.336 to 1.366 nats. Tested block and deletion checks retain a positive gain. Lower size cuts remove the gain. An early lognormal fit gives a slightly larger gain of 0.805 nats. The result supports a distribution forecast for this selected event class, but does not identify Brownian stress loading or a trigger. Catalog selection, incomplete coverage and six test intervals limit the result. No independent full sequence or new source is found. Code, aggregate evidence and exact external input hashes support reproduction without bundling the external catalog.
